thread:
alex: FYI: DCGM exporter alerts are noisy for a few nodes in eu-west-1. Getting a mix of Xid 12/31 and sporadic ECC correctable events. Oncall got paged twice in the last hour. Anyone else seeing this?

sre-bot: ALERT fired: dcgm_gpu_unhealthy_nodes (severity: warning) — 3 nodes in pool 'gpu-prod-eu-west-1'
  - summary: 'GPU health changes: XID errors and ECC correctable increments detected'

dan: Confirmed. I just checked the grafana dashboard — increase(dcgm_ecc_correctable_total[5m]) > 0 on 4 nodes, but most are +1 or +2 only. Xid errors are 1-3 each.

maria: Sounds like we're triggering on very transient noise. Current prometheus rule is basically any increase over 5m -> fire. That's too sensitive for correctable ECC or 1-off Xid. We should tune.

alex: Proposed quick wins:
 - treat "correctable ECC" as warning unless it crosses a higher rate threshold
 - require Xid errors > 5 within 15m to be critical (page)
 - add a cooldown (for: 10m) so transient spikes don't flood pages

lisa: +1. Also separate uncorrectable ECC and GPU reset/Xid categories. Uncorrectable should be immediate critical. Correctable -> threshold + sustained window.

maria: Drafted a prometheus rule snippet for recording + alerting. Will open a PR, but want feedback on thresholds before I push.

```yaml
# monitoring/prometheus/rules/gpu.rules.yaml (draft)
groups:
- name: gpu.rules
  rules:
  - record: gpu:correctable_ecc:rate5m
    expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_correctable_total[5m])
  - alert: GPUCorrectableECCHigh
    expr: gpu:correctable_ecc:rate5m > 5
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      summary: "High rate of correctable ECC errors on {{ $labels.instance }}"
      runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-xid"
    for: 10m
  - alert: GPUXidErrorsCritical
    expr: increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[15m]) > 5
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Repeated XID errors (>=6 in 15m) on {{ $labels.instance }} - consider drain/replace"
      playbook: "https://redwood.internal/playbooks/gpu-failure-triage"
    for: 5m
```

oncall-jamie: We also need automated ops actions for nodes that cross the critical thresholds. Proposal: annotate node then auto-drain with kube-drain-job if a label gpu:flaky=true and XidErrorsCritical triggers. Avoid auto-replace until we confirm persistent hardware fault.

dan: Agree on annotate->taint->drain flow. For the interim, we can silence the noisy warning alerts in eu-west-1 while we iterate.

maria: I'll open PR to monitoring repo with the rule above and add a recording rule to track 'gpu_flaky_count' per instance. PR description will include the runbook and proposed auto-drain playbook.

alex: Please set the warning alert to not page default on-call. Only critical should page. We can keep slack notifications for warning channel #gpu-alerts.

maria: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/monitoring/pull/342 — includes rule changes, runbook link, and explicit justification + test plan.

lisa: Nice. Can someone add a quick e2e test (promtool + dev cluster) before merging?

dan: I'll run promtool and push to staging alertmanager for A/B tomorrow. Also will add temporary silence for eu-west-1 for the noisy rule.

oncall-jamie: For hardware triage checklist (quick notes):
 - check nvml/dcgm logs for persistent Xid codes > 12
 - check dmesg for GPU resets
 - check ECC corrected vs uncorrected counts over 24h
 - if persistent uncorrectable -> take out of rotation and replace card
 - if only occasional correctable -> monitor and schedule for next maintenance window

alex: Perfect. Let's re-evaluate after the staging run. Meeting to sync: tomorrow 09:30 PST. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
